To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 26Al in CAIs most likely came from massive stars in a molecular cloud that formed the Sun; the 26Al abundance in the Sun's parent cloud was ~6 × 10–6, or 10-100 times higher than that in the interstellar medium (ISM); the Sun formed 4-7 Myr after the first generation of massive stars; and the Sun formed 10-50 Myr after the second generation of massive stars.

the Sun's 26Al and 41Ca were most likely inherited from the parent molecular cloud and were produced in a previous generation of stars, and that 60Fe was most likely inherited from a prior generation of supernovae.

(1) the presence of 41Ca in the early solar nebula requires that the Sun formed 4-6 million years after the massive stars whose winds contaminated the molecular cloud; (2) the presence of the SLRs 26Al, 41Ca and 60Fe in the early solar systems requires the formation of the Sun in a molecular cloud that had been contaminated by Wolf-Rayet wind from a previous generation of massive stars, with the Sun forming 4-5 Myr later
